decisions.decision: The chair will meet in person with the town manager next week to finalize and push forward the town hall/facilities survey.
The committee agreed to add a survey question asking residents how they use TC Pacios (storage, functions, voting) and where those uses would go if it closes.
Laura offered to convert the chair's draft survey document into a Google Form so responses can be compiled in a spreadsheet; the chair agreed to send her the document.
The committee set its next meeting for May 18th, keeping the first-and-third-Monday schedule.

The committee reaffirmed that its current charter is to investigate consolidating town administrative functions into one building, not to take on TC Pacios reuse as a new project without changing that charter.

minutes.headline: Committee weighs saving part of TC Pacios vs. town hall/Ritter consolidation, with no decision made
minutes.summary: The Municipal Building Design Committee discussed the fate of the vacated TC Pacios building -- whether any part of it (gym, kitchen, roof) is worth saving versus the committee's charter to consolidate town administrative functions into Ritter/Town Hall -- alongside an update on Turkey Hill Elementary's coming MSBA process. No formal votes were taken on substance; the committee agreed to refine and send out a facilities survey, add TC Pacios-related questions to it, and reconvene May 18th.

what_happened.line: The committee reaffirmed its charter is limited to studying a Ritter/Town Hall consolidation, not a TC Pacios reuse project, without voting to broaden it.
No vote was taken on whether any part of TC Pacios -- gym, kitchen, roof -- is worth saving.
The committee agreed to add questions to a resident survey asking how people use TC Pacios and where those uses would go if it closes.
A member offered to convert the chair's draft survey into a Google Form so responses can be compiled and reviewed.
The next meeting was set for May 18, continuing the first-and-third-Monday schedule.

why_it_matters: This touches whether the town keeps, repairs, or lets go of a building residents currently use for voting, long-term storage, and community functions like the gym and kitchen.
The resident survey being finalized will feed a planned fall town-meeting presentation on a town administration building, which residents would eventually vote on.
Members tied the discussion to the town's ongoing override vote, since facilities spending competes with school and other budget priorities.
